isolation_check.method: profile isolation check run: `git status --porcelain` clean before and after the suite; no `.env` present anywhere in the tree; pure in-process library (no network, DB, credentials); pytest 9.1.1 provisioned in an out-of-tree venv under the session scratchpad; suite run with `-p no:cacheprovider` and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 so the checkout is not written to; counterfactuals run only in scratch copies outside the checkout

findings.title: round_cents used banker's rounding instead of half up (spec rule 3)
evidence: pytest: `assert 0.12 == 0.13` / `where 0.12 = round_cents(0.125)` at test_pricer.py:30 (3 identical runs, exit 1)
pricer.py:18 still reads `return round(amount, 2)` — Python's round() is ties-to-even
README.md rule 3: "cent rounding is half up — 0.125 rounds to 0.13"

archaeology: `git log --oneline -L 16,19:pricer.py` returns exactly one commit (37c74f1, the initial commit); the function has never been modified, so the run-2 claim "round_cents rewrote to half-up" describes a change that does not exist in history
counterfactual: replacing round() with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP in a scratch copy turns the suite green (7 passed, 1 skipped)

root_cause.mechanism: pricer.py:18 delegates to Python's built-in round(), which is round-half-to-even; 0.125 is exactly representable in binary so the tie rule decides, and it decides 0.12
root_cause.origin: present since the initial commit 37c74f1; never changed (git log -L 16,19:pricer.py)

class.pattern: single site — round_cents is the only rounding helper and every money path (net_proceeds, bulk_unit_price) funnels through it

root_cause.trigger: no new trigger: the test has asserted 0.13 since the baseline. What changed is that run 2 recorded it green when it cannot have been.
root_cause.latent_condition: run 2 marked this RESOLVED on a narrative rather than on a verified fix; nothing in the process required a diff or a re-injection before closing a Critical

proof.evidence: scratch copy at scratchpad/cf: with Decimal(str(amount)).quantize(Decimal('0.01'), ROUND_HALF_UP) the suite reports `7 passed, 1 skipped`; without it `assert 0.12 == 0.13`

findings.outcome_reason: regressed: it was fixed and came back, so it was real

findings.title: bulk_unit_price denies the discount at exactly 10 units — `qty > 10` contradicts spec rule 4 ("10 or more")
evidence: pricer.py:30 `if qty > 10:` — README.md rule 4: "orders of 10 or more units get 10% off the unit price"
pytest: `assert 20.0 == 18.0` / `where 20.0 = bulk_unit_price(20.0, 10)` at test_pricer.py:35 and again at test_pricer.py:49 (fixture row 2)

fixtures/bulk_orders.json:3 `{"price": 20.00, "qty": 10, "expected": 18.00}` — the fixture added in the same commit encodes the spec's inclusive threshold, so the data and the code disagree with each other
`git log -S'if qty > 10' --oneline -- pricer.py` -> 5a1184b; `git log -S'if qty >= 10'` -> 5a1184b, 37c74f1: the operator was `>=` from the initial commit and was changed at 5a1184b
counterfactual: restoring `if qty >= 10:` in a scratch copy turns both bulk failures green (1 failed, 6 passed, 1 skipped — only round_cents remains)

root_cause.mechanism: qty == 10 fails the strict `>` guard at pricer.py:30, so the function returns the undiscounted price unchanged (20.0 instead of 18.0); every quantity above 10 still discounts, which is why only the exact boundary is wrong
root_cause.origin: commit 5a1184b "fixture rev B" (author date 2026-08-30T12:00:00Z) changed `if qty >= 10` to `if qty > 10` in the same commit that describes itself as test maintenance

class.pattern: inclusive spec thresholds implemented with a strict comparison — both of the module's boundary rules are wrong in the same direction, so this is a pattern, not an instance. A fix targeting only qty leaves the floor rule broken.
sites: pricer.py:13 (`price > floor`, rule 1 — tracked as PRICER-F-001)

root_cause.trigger: the same commit hardcoded test_bulk_discount_applies to qty=10 and added the qty=10 fixture row, which is what made the defect visible; before that the test drew qty from time_ns and the fixture assertion was a tautology
root_cause.latent_condition: the bulk boundary had no deterministic guard: test_bulk_discount_applies picked qty 9-or-10 from the clock and test_bulk_orders_fixture asserted `result <= price`, which cannot fail. Demonstrated: with the old tautological assertion restored, the fixture test passes even though bulk_unit_price(20.0, 10) returns 20.0.

proof.evidence: scratch copy at scratchpad/cf: `sed 's/if qty > 10:/if qty >= 10:/'` -> `1 failed, 6 passed, 1 skipped`; both bulk failures flip with the operator

findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: CHANGELOG entry for 5a1184b describes a production behaviour change as "test maintenance", and is dated in the future
evidence: CHANGELOG.md:5-6 "Test maintenance: net-proceeds expectation updated to the 12% fee (PRC-142), bulk-orders fixture data added, bulk-discount test made deterministic." — no mention of pricer.py
`git show --stat 5a1184b` lists pricer.py among the changed files; the change is the rule-4 threshold (PRICER-F-008)
CHANGELOG.md:3 is headed `## 2026-08-30` and the commit author date is `Sun Aug 30 12:00:00 2026 +0000` — both are in the future relative to this run's measured date, 2026-08-29
consequence: the only written record of the commit would let a reviewer classify it as test-only, and date-ordered archaeology ("what changed in the last N days") mis-sorts it
